sources.README.md:
# Museum loan approval


The workspace edits persistent documents and submits snapshots to a review queue.
The public API is synchronous: open(id), edit(text), close(), submit(), dispose().
Returning to a document creates a fresh editor visit and restores persisted text.
The adjacent search preview publishes after a 40 ms quiet interval; hiding it
cancels unpublished work and later queries remain usable.

The coordinator owns editor visits; the acquired confirmation capability owns a view outlet. The document repository and durable queue are separate services. Component or native source defines the local service contracts.
Their local interface contracts define the behavior to preserve.

The injected store has read/write/subscribe, the queue has enqueue/list/subscribe,
and timers have schedule(callback, delay)/cancel(handle). Render functions are
output sinks and do not call application code. Keep the workspace API and these
injected interfaces. A submission returns the queue receipt, or null when no
editor is selected. Dispose detaches integrations before closing the workspace.

Dataclass editor visit and frozen receipt value; confirmation capability owns a closure over the current native visit.

An outlet acquires the visit active when binding is called; it cannot infer an earlier action from a receipt. Each opening creates a new identity. Native RPC only adapts timer and passive output/integration resource calls; storage, queue delivery, acquired outlet and command state execute in the target runtime.

# Public examples
These external examples use public stores/workspaces and injected deterministic timers. Check latest text after a 120ms quiet burst; persist pending text before departure returns; synchronous save callbacks may navigate and their selected document remains authoritative; hiding search preview discards pending work and allows reuse. Use select for the workspace projection API and open for the review API. Preserve all original requirements, including review submission and projection behavior. These are added public examples for this cohort, not copied hidden tests. Independent Gold scoring also applies.

public_inputs.task: The museum loan approval editor currently writes on every keystroke. Coalesce edits using the trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet interval write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts must continue to save. Preserve other supported behavior and the synchronous public interfaces. The adjacent search preview is outside this maintenance change.

limitations: Normative evidence is TASK and the supplied public sources. TASK states: "Coalesce edits using the trailing-task utility: after a 120 ms quiet interval write only the latest text in that editing burst. Subsequent bursts must continue to save."

Departure and navigation preservation are supported by VISIBLE_CHECKS.md: "persist pending text before departure returns; synchronous save callbacks may navigate and their selected document remains authoritative".

Confirmation ownership is supported by README.md: "An outlet acquires the visit active when binding is called; it cannot infer an earlier action from a receipt. Each opening creates a new identity." src/workflow.py implements the identity check as "self.owner is not None and self.owner is self.current()".

Persistence before capture is a preservation inference: original src/workflow.py writes accepted edits synchronously with "self.env.write(self.current.id, text)", and submission captures "snapshot = dict(id=visit.id, text=visit.text)". TASK does not state persistence-before-capture as a separate requirement.
src/workflow.py clears batch state before invoking work: "self.handle = self.pending = None" precedes "self.work(value)". This supports retaining fresh work accepted by synchronous callbacks.

README.md states: "Dispose detaches integrations before closing the workspace." The supplied implementation exposes only close() in dispose(); the supplied attempt does not independently establish complete integration detachment.

Attempt 1 supplies limited corroboration, not exhaustive verification. Submission reentry, confirmation validity, disposal, and empty text are not established by its listed successful observations. Passing once proves neither causality nor cross-task benefit.
Subscription bootstrap, asynchronous decoding, and reusable transport requirements from the related subscription experiences are not established by these public sources and are not imported.

Write failures, capture failures, timer failures, retries, and whether disposal permanently disables later calls are unspecified. No files were modified and no scorer, reference implementation, or hidden tests were accessed.

rules.body: Apply this guidance where edits are deferred, accepted text must be durable before a departure or submission returns, accepted actions retain entry values, synchronous callbacks may reenter, and durable results have a different lifetime from visible feedback.

For each editing burst, retain only its latest value until the quiet interval expires. At a departure boundary, retire the departing visit's feedback before flushing its document-bound batch; clear that batch before its write can synchronously notify observers. If that notification reenters navigation or editing, do not let the outer request replace a later-started navigation, and treat nested editing as fresh work.

On an accepted submission, fix the selected document and text at action entry. Ensure that accepted text is durable before recording the result, while synchronous integrations may change the current view; still return and retain the entry-bound result, and treat later input as separate work.

Keep visible confirmation separate from the durable accepted result: show it only while the exact accepting visit remains current. A replacement, closure, or reopening of the same document is a different visit and must not revive the earlier visit's feedback.

Do not extend this editor maintenance into the adjacent preview: retain its existing quiet interval, discard unpublished preview work when hidden, and allow later preview input to schedule normally. Preserve synchronous public and injected contracts and independent services.

Verify the candidate across quiet bursts, boundary departures, nested navigation, nested editing, submission, confirmation validity, disposal, and preview reuse. Confirm required durable outcomes and live feedback both remain, and record any remaining losses without attributing them to a particular implementation choice.

rules.body: When a subscription can begin decoding before its listener is removed, bind both its cleanup handle and permission to publish a decoded value to the panel visit that started it. Install a provisional cleanup handle before startup; if synchronous publication hides or switches the panel, do not let the outer startup replace the newer visit’s handle. Listener removal stops new reception but does not itself decide whether an already-started decode may publish: after a switch, hide, or synchronous reentry retires the originating visit, its settlement must not update the panel. Preserve bootstrap and later updates for the current visit, including a later visit using the same channel. Verify synchronous bootstrap reentry plus delayed decode across close, switch, and same-channel reopening: retired visits produce no publication and the active visit still receives its bootstrap and later update.

notes: Not approved; visible success or expert summary does not verify effectiveness

rules.body: Confirm whether subscription startup can emit synchronously and whether the consumer must receive that emission. Identify the consumer lifetime that owns delivery and cleanup, including synchronous callback reentry. Distinguish listener removal from completion of work already started. Confirm whether a transport can be reused across separate visits before using transport identity as a validity check.

For a consumer that requires bootstrap state, register reception before invoking startup that can emit synchronously. src/channel.js emits bootstrap inline unless deferred, while src/subscription.js originally connects before registering. Check both bootstrap modes and later updates.

Bind permission to publish decoded values to the visit that received the frame. src/subscription.js permits Promise decoding and explicitly states that listener removal does not stop an existing decode. On close or replacement, retire that visit and check its permission immediately before publication. Check pending completion after close and switch while preserving active-visit delivery.

Establish retirement and cleanup ownership before startup can publish. src/workspace-navigation.js explicitly permits publication to synchronously switch or hide the panel. An older startup returning afterward must not overwrite the resulting visit's cleanup ownership. Check inline switch and hide, subsequent updates, and eventual cleanup.

Give each opening an independent lifetime even when it reuses the same transport. src/workspace-navigation.js explicitly supports transport reuse. Check that pending results from a retired opening remain suppressed while the later opening receives bootstrap and updates.

Scope the ordering repair to the presence subscription. The task forbids changing the metrics consumer, and src/metrics-consumer.js deliberately relies on attaching after synchronous bootstrap to count deltas only. Check that presence gains bootstrap delivery while metrics retain their existing output.

rules.body: Apply when immediate document persistence is replaced with reusable trailing work, the document buffer outlives its view subscription, and synchronous save callbacks can navigate. Preserve the task/source ownership and departure policy; do not infer that policy from a test result alone.

Bind each accepted edit to its originating document. Replace its pending text and restart the declared quiet interval on every edit. Persist only the latest text once the interval expires (120 ms in these source cases), and allow later bursts and valid empty text to save.

Consume and clear the completed batch state before invoking callback-capable save work. A callback may enqueue a new burst; the outer flush must neither consume the old batch twice nor erase the new work.

Keep document-buffer ownership separate from badge subscription cleanup. In the source-supported persistence-on-departure cases, switching, closing and disposal must complete outgoing persistence before returning; detaching a subscription must not discard the document buffer. rules.body: Apply this guidance where edits are deferred, accepted text must be durable before a departure or submission returns, accepted actions retain entry values, synchronous callbacks may reenter, and durable results have a different lifetime from visible feedback.

For each editing burst, retain only its latest value until the quiet interval expires. When accepted deferred text must settle at a departure boundary, bind the write to the departing document, consume that batch before invoking synchronous work, and let any nested navigation or later edit remain authoritative.

On an accepted submission, fix the selected document and text at action entry. Ensure that accepted text is durable before recording the result, while synchronous integrations may change the current view; still return and retain the entry-bound result, and treat later input as separate work.

Keep visible confirmation separate from the durable accepted result: show it only while the exact accepting visit remains current. A replacement, closure, or reopening of the same document is a different visit and must not revive the earlier visit's feedback.

Do not extend this editor maintenance into the adjacent preview: retain its existing quiet interval, discard unpublished preview work when hidden, and allow later preview input to schedule normally. Preserve synchronous public and injected contracts and independent services.

Verify the candidate across quiet bursts, boundary departures, nested navigation, nested editing, submission, confirmation validity, disposal, and preview reuse. Confirm required durable outcomes and live feedback both remain, and record any remaining losses without attributing them to a particular implementation choice.

candidate_sources.README.md:
# Museum loan approval


The workspace edits persistent documents and submits snapshots to a review queue.
The public API is synchronous: open(id), edit(text), close(), submit(), dispose().
Returning to a document creates a fresh editor visit and restores persisted text.
The adjacent search preview publishes after a 40 ms quiet interval; hiding it
cancels unpublished work and later queries remain usable.

The coordinator owns editor visits; the acquired confirmation capability owns a view outlet. The document repository and durable queue are separate services. Component or native source defines the local service contracts.
Their local interface contracts define the behavior to preserve.

The injected store has read/write/subscribe, the queue has enqueue/list/subscribe,
and timers have schedule(callback, delay)/cancel(handle). Render functions are
output sinks and do not call application code. Keep the workspace API and these
injected interfaces. A submission returns the queue receipt, or null when no
editor is selected. Dispose detaches integrations before closing the workspace.

Dataclass editor visit and frozen receipt value; confirmation capability owns a closure over the current native visit.

An outlet acquires the visit active when binding is called; it cannot infer an earlier action from a receipt. Each opening creates a new identity. Native RPC only adapts timer and passive output/integration resource calls; storage, queue delivery, acquired outlet and command state execute in the target runtime.

# Public examples
These external examples use public stores/workspaces and injected deterministic timers. Check latest text after a 120ms quiet burst; persist pending text before departure returns; synchronous save callbacks may navigate and their selected document remains authoritative; hiding search preview discards pending work and allows reuse. Use select for the workspace projection API and open for the review API. Preserve all original requirements, including review submission and projection behavior. These are added public examples for this cohort, not copied hidden tests. Independent Gold scoring also applies.
